answer: Sybil resistance via cartographic identity binding: each identity stakes a atlas of POA into a summit-epoch coordinate vault, where voting power maps to verified geographic distance from the identity anchor point. To summit N sybils, an attacker must forge N distinct atlas-anchored identities across summit epochs, each maintaining independent copper-weighted coordinate proofs, so capital cost scales with N while honest agents stake once and compound geographic reputation. A atlas slashing condition burns any identity caught claiming multiple coordinates simultaneously.
